trace_name: Claude Haiku 4.5 failed attempt to read SM59 RFC destinations

notes: This trace documents a highly inefficient and ultimately unsuccessful attempt to retrieve SM59 destinations.
Instead of using proper fairyfly tree-navigation commands, the model attempted JSON parsing, argument ordering mistakes, and session management failures.
The model did not consult the reference trace (sm59_destinations_openinference.json) beforehand, leading to reinvention of wheel and poor tool usage.
Session disconnected mid-exploration; no final destination list was produced.
This is a cautionary example of what NOT to do.

attributes.input.value: What SM59 connections does the system have?
attributes.output.value: Seven connection categories identified but no actual destination names retrieved. Session crashed.
attributes.failure_reason: Used wrong tool approach, argument ordering errors, no tree expansion method

attributes.tool.name: Bash
attributes.input.value: fairyfly session list; fairyfly connection list
attributes.mistake: Used Bash (POSIX) on Windows instead of PowerShell immediately

spans.name: Session launch with wrong connection management

attributes.tool.name: Fairyfly CLI
attributes.input.value: .\build\Release\fairyfly.exe session launch Bigfox; .\build\Release\fairyfly.exe transaction start SM59
attributes.output.value: Transaction start failed: 'This function is not possible'
attributes.mistake: Did not check if session needed login before attempting transaction

spans.name: Inefficient approach: Large JSON parsing from screen read

attributes.tool.name: Fairyfly CLI + PowerShell JSON parsing
attributes.input.value: .\build\Release\fairyfly.exe screen read --output json | ConvertFrom-Json | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 > sm59_screen.json
attributes.output.value: Saved 74.2KB JSON file containing full GUI dump
attributes.mistake: Dumped entire screen to file instead of using element-specific commands; then tried to parse nested JSON objects with wrong property names
subsequent_issues: Searched for row_count, column_count, rows properties that don't exist in GuiShell
Found GuiShell has tree_nodes but no children were populated
Spent multiple PowerShell calls trying to navigate tree structure without expanding nodes first

spans.name: Argument ordering errors in element click
spans.status_message: The following arguments were not expected: 3 --key

attributes.tool.name: Fairyfly CLI
attributes.mistake: Incorrect flag name (--key instead of --node-key) and wrong argument order; did not check CLI help before trying

attributes.tool.name: Fairyfly CLI
attributes.mistake: Attempted to double-click on tree without specifying which row/column (this is for GridView, not GuiShell trees)

attributes.tool.name: Fairyfly CLI
attributes.mistake: Session remained idle during lengthy JSON parsing and troubleshooting; SAP GUI likely timed out or connection was lost during exploration

attributes.tool.name: Fairyfly CLI
attributes.mistake: No connections remained; would have needed to re-launch session and start over from scratch

attributes.output.value: The correct approach was to use 'element get --list-nodes' and 'element click --tree-action expand', which were available but never discovered or used
lessons_learned: Did not read existing trace (sm59_destinations_openinference.json) which documented the exact workflow
Attempted JSON parsing of GUI dumps instead of using semantic CLI commands
Made multiple argument ordering and flag name errors without consulting CLI help first
Did not keep session active during exploration (long JSON parsing + troubleshooting)
Tried to use grid-based operations (--doubleclick --row --column) on a tree shell
Escalated from one failure to another instead of consulting documentation or reference traces
attributes.correct_approach: element get --list-nodes to read visible nodes, then element click --tree-action expand --node-key to expand each category systematically
